subject: SIG: follow-up - encryption controls, KMS/HSM evidence and rotation logs
messages:

Subject: SIG: encryption evidence request (in-transit, at-rest, KMS/HSM, rotation)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking the SIG. Security reviewed the encryption section and had a couple of follow-ups specific to key lifecycle and HSM usage for hosted vs. private deployments. High level asks:

- A short narrative of how data is encrypted at-rest (DEK/KEK/envelope encryption) and how CMKs are used.
- Confirmation of TLS versions/ciphers in-transit and whether mutual TLS is enforced for private deployments.
- KMS/HSM: which cloud HSMs are supported (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, GCP CMEK, Azure), and whether Redwood uses HSM-backed keys for hosted CMKs.
- Key rotation: logs or a rotation report for the last 12 months (sample), and the automated rotation policy for service-managed keys.

Can you provide a short cover note answering the bullets above and the rotation log CSV for our records? If you can attach a sample CloudTrail extract (or equivalent) and any HSM attestation we can reference in our vendor review, that would be ideal.

Goal is to have this bundled into the SIG file by EOD on Friday (2026-05-14) if possible — procurement wants an initial go/no-go.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior InfoSec Analyst
FinApps

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG: encryption evidence request (in-transit, at-rest, KMS/HSM, rotation)

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary (we will attach a concise answers PDF and evidence files shortly):

- At-rest: Redwood uses envelope encryption. Each tenant/object is encrypted with a data encryption key (DEK) using AES-256-GCM. DEKs are wrapped by a customer or service-managed master key (CMK) stored in the customer's selected KMS (AWS KMS by default for hosted). Wrapped keys are stored with the object metadata; unwrapped keys are never persisted in plaintext.

- In-transit: All network traffic to our hosted API endpoints uses TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites; we prefer TLS 1.3 where supported. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we support mutual TLS for service-to-service and customer endpoint authentication. Certificate rotation for hosted endpoints is automated (ACME-like flow) and certificates are rotated at least every 90 days.

- KMS/HSM: Hosted: CMKs are managed in AWS KMS (HSM-backed) by default. Customers on Dedicated/Private can bring their own CMK from AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or Azure Key Vault; we also integrate with CloudHSM where customers require HSM-backed key material. For customers that need on-prem HSMs we support external HSM integrations and provide attestations where available.

- Key rotation & evidence: Service-managed CMKs have automated annual rotation; DEKs are rotated per lifecycle policies and re-encrypted when keys are rotated. For customers using customer-managed keys, rotation is controlled by the customer's KMS policy. Attached: a rotation report CSV (sample last 12 months), a short answers PDF for the SIG encryption section, a CloudTrail sample extract showing KMS GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt events, and our latest HSM attestation (redacted PII).

Neha — can you confirm the attached CSV matches our CloudTrail export and that the HSM attestation is the latest? Soojin — please confirm the wording on mutual TLS support for Private deployments (I kept it high level).

-Marcus

Hi all — attaching the evidence bundle per Marcus' summary. Brief notes to accompany attachments:

1) redwood_sig_encryption_section_answers_v1.2.pdf — concise narrative you can paste into the SIG. Includes architecture diagram (DEK/KEK flow) and a table of supported KMS/HSM options.

2) redwood_kms_rotation_report_2025-06_to_2026-05.csv — generated from CloudTrail + internal key-management audit. Columns: timestamp, action (CreateKey/RotateKey/GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/DisableKey), key_id (redacted), principal, region. We redacted principals to service accounts only. This is a sample for reviewer consumption; full logs can be shared under NDA.

3) sample_cloudtrail_kms_events.txt — small extract showing GenerateDataKey and Decrypt calls tied to tokenized request IDs.

4) hsm_attestation_redwood_20251120.pdf — third-party attestation for our use of AWS CloudHSM for hosted CMKs (redacted).

Soojin — wording check on mTLS: we support mutual TLS for inter-service auth and for Private deployments we can enable client certificate validation at the edge/gateway. We also support mTLS between internal services using SPIFFE identities where customers deploy our private control plane.

Elena — if you need a signed cover letter on company letterhead summarizing these controls, I can run that through legal and send a one-page PDF.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
